mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of the foreign institutional shareholder's Certificate of Incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the instrument in the country of issuance, then apply only one of the following routes: (A) Hague Apostille if the issuing state is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, obtain a single apostille from the competent authority of that state (e.g., China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial foreign affairs office); or (B) Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Party, authenticate the notarized instrument directly at the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction over that state. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must screen every shareholder, director, UBO, and authorized signatory against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) OFAC 50 Percent Rule derivative listings; (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (v) Korean Government sanctions designations administered by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit; (vi) UK HMT sanctions list; and (vii) open-source adverse media, PEP registers, Interpol notices, and domestic Korean criminal and sanctions databases. Any PEP, family member, or close associate requires senior compliance approval before filing. Negative sanctions hits trigger immediate Suspicious Transaction Report to KoFIU. The entire screening must be repeated within 48 hours prior to registration and again before bank account onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IROS) electronic registration portal (www.iros.go.kr) and the local District Court registration division
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Hangeul; if the desired name is a foreign word, it must be transliterated into Hangeul using standard phonetic conversion rules, with the original foreign spelling listed as a non-controlling secondary business name. The four-tier naming doctrine requires: (1) a distinctive element that is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered trade name; (2) a business object or industry descriptor; (3) the entity-ending 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock corporation); and (4) an optional parallel English or Romanized trade name for cross-border e-commerce. Hanja representations are allowed only where the registration court accepts the word as a phonetically corresponding legal trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the registry court issues a written refusal notice. The applicant may, within 14 days, file an immediate appeal with the appellate division of the district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act, or file a fresh application with an amended distinctive element. The appeal must annex a comparative name search report, legal argument that the proposed name is neither identical nor materially misleading, Hangeul transliteration certificates, and evidence of prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token. The court is required to decide within 14 days after submission; if the appeal is denied, a clean new name should be selected and the registration procedure restarted with a newly notarized board resolution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by the National Tax Service (NTS) and Korean banks for this retail e-commerce industry unless it is a service-enabled co-working or office floor with an exclusive lease or dedicated desk, normal business records such as tax invoices, contracts, and board minutes are accessible, and a responsible employee or licensed agent is present during business hours. A pure mail-drop address without physical business substance will be refused for VAT registration and corporate bank account opening. Shared offices with management services can satisfy the place-of-business test only if supported by written management/lease agreements and local substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: the District Tax Office may inspect (i) the registered office signboard, lease, and desk space; (ii) books, electronic tax invoices, and VAT returns; (iii) employment and labor records and responsible-person presence; (iv) board and shareholder meeting minutes; and (v) bank mandates and transaction documentation. For a low-risk online retailer of outdoor camping equipment, the quantified risk of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months is approximately 15-25 percent; if the address is a pure mail-forwarding mailbox or the company files zero-turnover VAT returns, the risk rises to 65-75 percent. Maintain full original documentation at the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book III, Chapter II, Articles 289, 291, 292, 295, 300, 302 and 317; Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 4 through 6; Registration and License Tax Act Article 27; Commercial Registration Act and Commercial Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (operationally accessible through the Supreme Court of Korea I-REG online registration system); foreign investment reporting handled by KOTRA Invest KOREA One-Stop service or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa together with the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) in the form prescribed by the Commercial Registration Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act. A Chusik Hoesa may be formed with zero or nominal paid-in capital, and no statutory blocked escrow account rule applies. However, paid-in capital must be actually deposited in a Korean bank account opened for the company in the course of incorporation and evidenced by a certificate of deposit or paid-in capital certificate; withdrawals after registration are subject to the capital maintenance and creditor protection rules of the Commercial Act. If foreign-invested enterprise status is sought under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the foreign investor must hold at least 10% voting ownership and invest at least KRW 100,000,000, and the funds must be remitted into Korea through a licensed foreign exchange channel. The USD fee shown is an indicative conversion of the KRW-denominated registration license tax for a KRW 100,000,000 paid-in capital, including the 20% education surtax and court filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION. This meeting of the board of directors of [Company], a Chusik Hoesa under formation under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, was duly convened and held on [date]; all directors received notice, a quorum was present, and the following resolutions were adopted by unanimous vote. RESOLVED, that the board of directors hereby ratifies, adopts, and approves the subscription and issuance of [number] ordinary shares of class [class] at a subscription price of [amount] Korean won per share to the subscribers shown in the subscription statement; the board confirms that the aggregate paid-in capital has been received in the company's incorporation deposit account and certified by the depositary bank; and the board directs that the paid-in capital be transferred to the corporate operating account after incorporation registration is completed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [address], Republic of Korea; the representative director and the corporate secretary are directed to file the head office registration with the competent district court Commercial Registration Office and to keep all statutory books, seals, and records at that address. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the board authorizes the opening and maintenance of deposit, foreign exchange, merchant, settlement, and payment processing bank accounts at banks selected by management; any two of the representative director, chief financial officer, and corporate secretary shall act as authorized signatories for withdrawals, transfers, and payment instructions; and all banking mandates shall be governed by the corporate seal and must incorporate anti-money-laundering and maker-checker controls. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the board appoints [name] as representative director and chief executive officer, [name] as chief financial officer, and [name] as corporate secretary and non-executive director, each to serve until the next annual general meeting and until a qualified successor is elected; the board delegates to the chief executive officer and corporate secretary authority to execute incorporation filings, foreign investment reports, NTS tax registrations, employment agreements, website terms, privacy policies, and commercial contracts. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the board approves all ordinary course activities required for internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping equipment, including e-commerce platform operation, payment gateway contracting, customer refunds, consumer protection compliance, logistics service agreements, and marketing arrangements, and ratifies the actions of the incorporators in preparing, executing, and notarizing the articles of incorporation. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption, shall be inserted in the corporate minute book, and shall be furnished to banks, auditors, and regulatory agencies upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Reserve the Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public in the Republic of Korea (Korean Association of Notaries) and Supreme Court of Korea corporate name search service through I-REG
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name availability search for the proposed Korean corporate name on the Supreme Court of Korea's I-REG service, avoiding names identical or deceptively similar to existing registered companies and brands. Prepare the articles of incorporation containing the corporate name, the precise objective of internet retailing of outdoor sports and camping equipment, the number and par value of authorized shares, the type of shares issued to the initial subscribers, the method of public announcement, and the registered office municipality. Under Article 292 of the Korean Commercial Act, the articles must be notarized before registration; the incorporators must sign or hand-mark the articles in the notary's presence. The same meeting should produce incorporators' minutes or written consent evidence, confirming appointment of the initial statutory officers. If a foreign investor is participating, also prepare a power of attorney in bilingual form and translated identity documents. The notary will stamp the notarized duplicate, which becomes part of the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and name search result
Notarizable English-Korean Articles of Incorporation draft
Passport or national identity card of each incorporator
Alien Registration Number or foreign investor identification number (if foreign)
Power of attorney for the local incorporator (if foreign incorporators are absent)
Registered office lease contract or deposit on a nominated address
Statement of initial shares subscribed and paid-in capital amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is rejected for similarity, select a secondary name and re-run the search without additional substantive submission. If the notary identifies civil-law or typographical defects, correct the draft, re-execute signatures, and re-notarize; the cure typically takes one additional business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Incorporation Deposit Account and Pay In Capital at a Licensed Korean Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Depository commercial bank authorized in Korea under the Banking Act; for foreign investment remittance, a foreign exchange bank licensed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the notarized articles of incorporation, present a request to the bank to open a temporary or incorporation-purpose deposit account in the name of the company being incorporated. The incorporators must deposit the full subscribed capital into this account and obtain a certificate of paid-in capital or deposit balance certificate issued by the bank. If the investment is foreign-sourced, the investor must remit the funds from an overseas account through customary foreign exchange procedures and preserve the foreign exchange remittance certificate, since this certificate will support a later foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The bank will conduct customer due diligence and source-of-wealth checks; accordingly, provide bank statements, tax returns, or business licences evidencing lawful origin of funds. The certificate of paid-in capital should be issued in both Korean and English if needed by the registry, and it must show the exact paid-in amount, account number, and the company's name as account holder. Do not withdraw the deposited funds before incorporation registration, as the registry requires a current certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized articles of incorporation
Incorporators' identification documents
Corporate name and corporate seal plan
Proof of lawful source of funds for shareholders
Lease agreement or address documentation for the registered office
Completed bank account application forms and anti-money-laundering declaration
Foreign exchange remittance certificate (if investment is from outside Korea)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, submit certified bank statements, gift or inheritance evidence, or audited financial statements. If account opening is refused, another licensed bank may be selected, and the same capital deposit certificate procedure can be repeated without losing the notarized articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Foreign Investment Report and Obtain Foreign Investment Certificate for Foreign-Shareholding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest KOREA One-Stop Service Center, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the Chusik Hoesa will be owned by a non-resident holding at least 10% voting equity and investing at least KRW 100,000,000, file a foreign investment report with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank before the capital is remitted, or if the subscription has already been completed, file the applicable acquisition report within the statutory deadline. Submit the prescribed report forms together with the foreign investor's identity document, a certified Korean translation if necessary, the notarized articles of incorporation, and the deposit certificate from the bank. The report will be processed by the foreign exchange bank or forwarded to KOTRA, and the agency will issue a foreign investment report certificate. This certificate is essential for future dividend remittance, capital repatriation, tax benefits, and visa procedures for foreign directors. Obtain a separate foreign investment business registration certificate after incorporation if the company will engage in a restricted industry; outdoor camping equipment internet retailing is not restricted, so the ordinary report procedure applies. Keep a complete file of all report documents because the commercial registry and immigration authority may request them.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form prescribed by FIPA
Passport or national identity card of each foreign investor
Power of attorney for local counsel or representative
Notarized articles of incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital or deposit balance
Foreign exchange remittance certificate with exchange receipt
Foreign investor identification number (if already assigned)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the report is returned due to incomplete documentation, use the KOTRA online correction channel to attach the omitted evidence and resubmit within the statutory window; if the investment was made before the report, an acquisition report can be filed within the legally permitted post-acquisition period, and professional counsel should be engaged to regularize timing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the District Court Commercial Registration Office and Pay Registration Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Supreme Court of Korea I-REG e-registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation within the statutory period. The registration must include the notarized articles of incorporation, the certificate of paid-in capital issued by the bank, written acceptance of office by directors and representative director, the certificate of foreign investment report (if applicable), consent of the lessor for the registered office, and the certificate of corporate seal. Recompute the registration license tax under the Registration and License Tax Act: generally 0.4% of paid-in capital with a statutory minimum, plus a 20% education surtax and the court filing fee. Pay the assessed tax before or at submission and present the payment receipt to the registry. The court registrar will review the application, check for legal compliance, and, upon approval, issue the certificate of registered matters and open the corporate registration record. The company is legally incorporated as of the moment the location of its head office is entered in the commercial register. After registration, obtain the corporate seal registration certificate and the company registration certificate, which serve as proof of legal existence for banks and payment processors.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation in the prescribed commercial register form
Notarized articles of incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital or deposit balance issued by a Korean bank
Written consent and report on appointment of directors and representative director
Certificate of foreign investment report (if foreign-owned)
Consent of building owner to use the registered office address
Payment receipts for registration license tax, education surtax, and court fee
Power of attorney if filed by a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order or rejects the filing, review the omission in the order, prepare a supplementary filing using the same application number, and resubmit within two weeks; a rejected filing does not require a fully new application if the original receipt is preserved. If the capital certificate has expired, obtain a refreshed balance certificate from the bank before resubmission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the electronic filing and registration portal HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance is executed through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS portal (https://unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A domestic Chusik Hoesa must apply to the competent district tax office for a 10-digit Business Registration Number (TIN) within 20 days of commencing business, using the HomeTax business registration application and supplying the articles of incorporation, business premises documentation, foreign shareholder proof if applicable, and identification of the legal representative; the district tax office issues the Business Registration Certificate, which serves as the single Taxpayer Identification Number for Corporate Tax, Value-Added Tax, and withholding purposes. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business that is nevertheless required to charge Korean VAT, the entity must complete non-resident business operator registration on HomeTax before the first taxable supply, appoint a domestic tax representative under Article 82 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, and obtain a 10-digit registration number in the same format; no minimum capital or Korean incorporation is required for that VAT registration. If the non-resident entity later establishes a fixed Korean place of business, it converts to the ordinary district tax office registration procedure. Foreign ownership of a Chusik Hoesa does not create any separate foreign shareholder TIN requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Korean tax law. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically a non-transparent domestic corporation taxable at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. Qualifying Korean resident controlled groups may elect consolidated corporation tax for wholly-owned subsidiaries, but this election does not create pass-through treatment; no hybrid mismatch or US-style check-the-box election is available as a voluntary classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80,000,000 of annual taxable turnover for classification as an ordinary taxable person under the Value-Added Tax Act; however, VAT registration with the National Tax Service is mandatory from business commencement for any business making taxable supplies, so the KRW 80 million threshold affects simplified-taxpayer status rather than the existence of a VAT registration obligation. A foreign non-resident e-commerce seller with no Korean establishment is required to register for Korean VAT in respect of continuing cross-border taxable supplies made to Korean recipients.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea does not operate a Latin American-style pre-clearance invoice authorization model; its statutory real-time fiscal control is the Electronic Tax Invoice (e-Tax Invoice) transmitted to NTS HomeTax. B2B e-Tax Invoices and all tax invoices issued by corporations must be transmitted to NTS by the day following the supply date through HomeTax, an approved ASP/VAN service, or the HomeTax open API. Each e-Tax Invoice carries a government-serialised invoice number and digital metadata (business registration numbers, supply value, and VAT) used for anti-fraud matching. For B2C internet retail, credit card and cash-receipt transaction data are transmitted to NTS directly by payment card acquirers and registered cash receipt agents, functioning as the Korean consumer-phase anti-fraud stamping mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, goods exported to a foreign place are zero-rated if: (i) the goods are shipped from Korea under an export declaration filed with Korea Customs Service; (ii) the KCS export declaration identifies the Chusik Hoesa as the exporter; (iii) the export price is actually received in foreign currency within the statutory settlement period; and (iv) the transaction is substantiated by the underlying sale, shipment, and payment documentation. For internet retail of outdoor camping equipment sold through Stripe or PayPal, each parcel must be cleared by KCS as an export and the underlying payment must be evidenced as foreign-currency export earnings. Input VAT attributable to the exported goods is creditable, and any excess refund is settled through the VAT return. Digital services or services incidental to exported goods are zero-rated only to the extent they are performed wholly outside Korea and received by a non-resident recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Export Shipment Report accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, including the Certificate of Export Clearance
Commercial Invoice and export purchase order or contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international courier waybill forming the transport evidence for the exported parcel
Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate issued by a designated foreign exchange bank, evidencing the inward remittance and sale/purchase of the export proceeds
Stripe/PayPal settlement reports linked to the foreign buyer and confirming collection of net export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating is scrutinised against the KCS export declaration, the transport evidence, and the foreign exchange settlement record. If the export declaration is absent, false, cancelled, or if the export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 18-month period, NTS will claw back the 0% rate, assess output VAT of 10% on the net supply value, and add non-report or underreport additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including an enhanced additional tax of 40% for fraudulent or grossly negligent presentation. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may result in imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to three times the tax evaded. Korea Customs Service and Bank of Korea/Foreign Exchange Bank penalty rules may also apply for false export declarations and late settlement of export proceeds. The tax assessment period may be reopened for up to five years for ordinary cases and up to ten years for fraudulent or intentionally concealed export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; operational oversight by the Korea Customs Service for trade settlement reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including cross-border trade settlements, service fees, and profit remittances, subject to mandatory reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) administered by the Bank of Korea. Capital account transactions are largely liberalized but require filing or declaration depending on the type and amount, particularly for foreign direct investment, borrowing, and securities transactions. There is no general surrender requirement compelling exporters to convert all foreign currency receipts into KRW; however, exporters must repatriate proceeds within a statutory period and report the receipt to a designated foreign exchange bank. For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment, inbound equity injections from non-resident shareholders, import payments for inventory, and outbound profit distributions are permissible without prior approval, but must be supported by underlying transaction documentation and routed through a Korean Won or foreign currency account at a domestic licensed bank. Practical hurdles include bank-level compliance reviews for large remittances, Korea Customs Service reconciliation for import/export settlements, and potential transfer-pricing scrutiny on cross-border payments to related parties. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) oversees licensing, and the Bank of Korea requires that any foreign exchange transaction exceeding USD 5,000 be reported, while transactions above USD 50,000 may require a certificate of receipt or a foreign exchange purchase/sale contract. Profit remittance by a foreign-owned entity is not subject to withholding on dividends beyond the standard 22% corporate-level tax and 20-22% dividend withholding tax if a tax treaty rate does not apply, but the remitting bank will require evidence of tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a board resolution declaring the dividend. Overall, the regime is business-friendly but documentation-heavy, and treasury operations must be built on traceable, bank-verified rails rather than unregulated fintech intermediaries.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea does not impose a mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; however, under Article 16 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related BOK regulations, exporters must repatriate foreign currency receipts within 18 months from the date of export declaration. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts at domestic banks, but the export proceeds must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days of receipt using the Electronic Import/Export Transaction Report. For goods sold through internet retailing, the e-commerce operator may receive settlement through payment aggregators such as Stripe or PayPal; these funds must ultimately be wired to a Korean domestic foreign currency account as a trade settlement, with the underlying shipping documents, customs declarations, and payment gateway settlement statements preserved for bank verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Corporate Current Account and Foreign Currency Account for Import Settlements
Operational Account for Small and Medium Enterprise E-commerce

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for primary treasury operations. South Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires all cross-border payments and receipts to be conducted through a licensed foreign exchange bank operating in Korea. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer, or multi-currency virtual IBAN providers are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) to hold KRW or provide domestic Korean won accounts. They cannot issue local KRW account numbers that are connected to the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute (KFTC) Won Clearing System, nor can they authenticate FEIS filings. Foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa entities must therefore maintain a primary corporate account at a domestic Tier-1 bank. A global EMI may be used as an auxiliary collection wallet for foreign card payments, but settlement from Stripe, PayPal, or Shopify Payments must be swept into the Korean bank account within mandated reporting windows; legal exposure arises if the EMI is used to circumvent BOK reporting or to park export proceeds beyond the 18-month repatriation window. The recommended architecture is domestic KRW account plus one foreign currency account at the same bank, with Stripe/PayPal settlement via SWIFT to that foreign currency account, then a bank-brokered conversion to KRW with FEIS reporting by the bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required for the statutory director and signatories during corporate account opening. In practice, Korean Tier-1 banks follow the 'Real-name Financial Transaction Act' and will require the statutory director to appear at a domestic branch with original corporate seal (hongin), corporate registration certificate, and personal identification. The foreign director who cannot travel to Korea may request a remote interview via the bank's global desk and a notarized power of attorney appointing a resident Korea-based co-signatory, but most banks will still require at least one authorized signatory with a Korean resident registration number or alien registration card to be physically present. Consular proxy opening is only available from the bank's overseas branch if the bank maintains a branch in the director's country; otherwise, the KYC acceptance is Low. For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident ownership, a practical onboarding path is: director obtains a short-term business visa, schedules a three-day trip, appears at Shinhan or Hana's Global Banking Center in Seoul, presents original documents with apostilled certificates, and completes the interview on-site.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident sole director and shareholder with no Korean credit history or local tax footprint, flagged as a shell corporate structure despite the entity being a domestic Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide apostilled certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, proof of registered business address either as a long-term lease or owned office in Korea, a detailed group structure chart showing ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with over 25% ownership, UBO passport and proof of residential address, board resolution authorizing account opening, and a substantive business plan demonstrating e-commerce operations, including supplier contracts, logistics agreements, and projected transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments from high-risk payment aggregators (Stripe, PayPal) with cross-border card traffic and diffuse counterparty jurisdictions, creating uncertainty regarding the source of funds and trade-settlement legitimacy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit monthly payout statements from Stripe and PayPal for at least three months or, for a newly formed entity, the signed merchant agreements and settlement schedules; provide end-customer transaction records and refund history; map each payout to customs declarations and import purchase invoices; and prepare an internal AML policy or use of a licensed third-party AML compliance vendor to perform transaction monitoring on digital sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Imported inventory financing pattern with large purchase payments to suppliers in China and Vietnam via Hong Kong intermediary accounts, a common trade-based money laundering typology.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver full supply chain documentation comprising proforma invoices, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or air waybills, Korea Customs Service import declarations (import clearance numbers), and bank payment orders showing a logical chain from the corporate account to the actual supplier; obtain a letter from the Korean shipping/customs broker verifying goods movements; and maintain a transfer-pricing file if any related party is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid anticipated revenue growth projected in the business plan with insufficient initial capitalization for a low-risk e-commerce operator; banks may question the economic substance and treatment of shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a capital injection plan with funds remitted from the shareholder's verified personal or corporate account, not from obscure shell accounts; present a cash flow forecast with realistic gross margin assumptions; execute a formal loan agreement if funds are structured as shareholder loans and declare the loan to the Bank of Korea through the designated foreign exchange bank; additionally submit board minutes approving the funding structure and the company's anticipated annual revenue split by channel.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be conducted through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A non-resident shareholder remitting share capital or shareholder loans should wire USD, EUR, or KRW from an account in their country of residence via SWIFT MT103 to the Chusik Hoesa's foreign currency or KRW capital escrow account at Shinhan, Hana, Woori, or Kookmin. Upon receipt, the bank requires the entity to submit the Foreign Investment Report and a capital contribution receipt proof; when the foreign equity ratio is at least 10% and the investment exceeds KRW 100 million, a Foreign Investment Reporting Certificate from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy must be filed within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. For smaller investments, a declaration with the bank can be made. Purpose codes must reflect 'Direct investment in corporations' or 'Foreign direct investment equity investment' under the BOK's transaction classification; never use personal gift or remittance codes. After the funds are credited, the bank will issue a certificate of foreign currency receipt, and the entity must complete registration of capital by filing the financial statements to the tax authority and the BOK's FEIS within the prescribed window. The source of funds should be wired from the UBO's personal or corporate account with documentary evidence of the same name to avoid a fat-finger mismatch or third-party fund structure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the online retailing of outdoor camping equipment consist of (1) import settlement to overseas brand manufacturers or wholesalers and (2) operational payments such as digital advertising, shipping, logistics, and software subscriptions. Import payments must be made through SWIFT MT103 from the entity's domestic foreign currency account, with the bank filing an Import Payment Declaration using the Electronic Import/Export Transaction Report; the Korea Customs Service will match the payment to the import declaration number. Commercial letters of credit can be used for high-value or recurring supplier relationships, but for a low-risk e-commerce company that purchases finished goods in small- and medium-sized batches, an MT103 telegraphic transfer with open account terms is more efficient and cheaper. Documentary collections are permissible but rarely advised in e-commerce because physical documents lag behind digital inventory. All outbound payments under USD 50,000 may be processed by the bank with simplified due diligence; above that threshold, the bank will request the invoice, import declaration, and supplier registration certificate. The Finance Supervisory Service also recommends that companies maintain a bank-approved payment calendar to avoid triggering multiple-same-day payments which can be flagged as structuring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward trades (foreign exchange forward contract) between KRW and USD/EUR/JPY for hedging real trade receivables and payables, allowed only up to 100% of the underlying transaction amount with a mandatory tie to documentary trade evidence.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW: not permitted domestically for KRW because KRW is an onshore deliverable currency; offshore NDF markets for KRW are accessible only to licensed institutions and cannot be used by a Korean operating entity without breaching BOK derivative position limits, so the treasury should avoid attempting onshore NDFs.

Cross-currency swaps (KRW/USD or KRW/EUR) for matching long-term import supply agreements or foreign currency borrowings, permitted when the swap notional is supported by a real trade debt with a maturity aligned to the underlying settlement date.

Plain-vanilla FX options (call and put) on USD/KRW and EUR/KRW for hedging contingent payment obligations through a Korean bank's dealing desk, requiring a signed ISDA master agreement or a Korean Financial Investment Association standard master agreement.
No uncovered speculative derivative positions are allowed; all hedging must be covered by underlying trade transactions under the Bank of Korea's foreign exchange position management rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and financial statement approval (annual settlement of accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate body; minutes and supporting resolutions are retained at the registered office and any registered changes in officers are filed with the Korean Court Registry Office (local district court).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e. by 31 March for a calendar-year corporation; registrar notification of officer changes is due within two weeks of the resolution (30 days if the change took place overseas).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register an officer change within 14 days subjects the responsible director or joint representative to an administrative fine under the Commercial Act (up to KRW 5,000,000); the omission also prevents the company from asserting the change against bona fide third parties; persistent failure to hold the AGM may prompt a shareholder derivative action or court-ordered dissolution for deadlock.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (corporate tax base and tax amount report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system; filing office is the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered principal place of business.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a fiscal year ending 31 December the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or understatement triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the underdeclared tax (40 percent for fraudulent concealment or a non-filed return) plus delinquency interest at 0.03 percent per day (approximately 10.95 percent per annum); continued non-payment can lead to seizure of bank accounts and receivables and cancellation of the business registration by the NTS for tax purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (provincial/city corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (province, city or county) via the NTS HomeTax system, which transfers the return to the relevant local tax authority.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year and, for a calendar-year company, by 30 April of the following year (the local return can be filed after the national corporate return is finalised).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a local corporate income tax return attracts an additional local tax equal to 20 percent of the unpaid local corporate income tax, and delinquency interest accrues daily at the local tax delinquency rate (currently 0.03 percent per day as prescribed annually); extended non-payment is enforced by attachment and public auction of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax return for the preceding half-year tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year (January-June): due 25 July of the same year; second half-year (July-December): due 25 January of the following year; preliminary quarterly returns are due 25 April and 25 October respectively.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or filing a false return triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the omitted VAT (40 percent in case of concealment or fraud), plus daily delinquency interest at 0.03 percent per day; after two consecutive non-filing periods the NTS may order closure of the business place, which for a dormant e-commerce operation can cause cancellation of the relevant taxable business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: For a Chusik Hoesa meeting the audit threshold under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies: the external auditor reports to the board and shareholders; the audited financial statements are attached to the corporate tax return and are made available for disclosure on the Financial Supervisory Service DART system where required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external audit must be completed and the audit report submitted in time for approval at the annual general meeting, which must occur by 31 March for a calendar-year company; the audited financial statements must accompany the NTS corporate tax return filed by the same date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company subject to mandatory external audit that fails to appoint an external auditor within the statutory period is exposed to a court order appointing an auditor, an administrative fine under the External Audit Act, and regulatory referral to the Financial Supervisory Commission; falsifying audit documents can lead to criminal prosecution and significant monetary fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Chusik Hoesa incorporated under Korean law, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory if: (i) the company is a listed issuer or has securities publicly traded in Korea; (ii) as at the close of the previous fiscal year, total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.6 million) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; (iii) the company is designated by the Financial Services Commission or the Securities and Futures Commission due to suspected accounting irregularities or as a condition of a regulatory order; (iv) the company belongs to finance, insurance, holding company or public-interest categories set out in the Act; or (v) the company is otherwise classified as a large unlisted company and meets statutory large-company asset or revenue indicators. Entities below the asset threshold are generally exempt from mandatory statutory audit unless their shareholders holding at least 20 percent of the voting shares apply to the court to appoint an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea has adopted Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies and for entities required to undergo statutory external audits; non-listed small and medium companies may elect Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP / SME accounting standards) for statutory financial reporting. For multinational groups, the Korean statutory accounts must still be prepared separately under the applicable Korean framework, and IFRS consolidation principles may apply at the ultimate parent level.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a single annual UBO confirmation or annual return for a private Chusik Hoesa; the permanent statutory obligations are: (i) the company must keep a complete register of members (shareholder ledger) recording the name, address, number of shares, kind/class of shares and date of acquisition of every registered shareholder; (ii) any transfer of shares takes effect only after the transferee's name and detail are entered in the register; (iii) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested enterprise must report any subsequent change in foreign ownership or shareholding structure to the appropriate delegated authority within 30 days of the event; and (iv) the register of directors, the register of charges or encumbrances and the minute book must be kept at the registered office and be open for inspection by shareholders or directors during business hours. There is no fixed annual certification filing unless the entity is subject to the external audit regime, in which case the auditor will inspect these registers as part of the audit.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 12,000 per annum for a mandatory statutory audit; USD 1,500 - USD 6,000 for a non-audited compilation/review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top national marginal rate plus 10% local income tax surtax on the tax payable, producing a combined top marginal rate of 26.4%; progressive brackets of 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for ordinary e-commerce retailers; available reductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act: R&D tax credits (up to 25% for SMEs), job-creation tax credits (up to KRW 14.7 million per new regular employee), SME Venture Start-up corporate tax reduction (50% for up to 5 years for qualifying venture companies in special zones), and facility investment tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on taxable income and tax amount (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서, official Form 1) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end; automatically extended to the next business day where the deadline falls on a weekend or public holiday).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number and legal name of the Chusik Hoesa as registered with the competent tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested Korean corporation uses the Korean business registration number; a foreign corporation without a domestic place of business uses the foreign corporate identification reference assigned by the NTS for Korean-source income withholding returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Fiscal Year and Reporting Period (사업연도)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year to which the return relates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the same period as the domestic fiscal year; in a short-period or liquidation return, precise beginning and termination dates must be stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate adjusted taxable income after applying loss carryforwards, nontaxable income, and deductions permissible under the Corporate Income Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Domestic-source income taxable in Korea is limited to the categories enumerated in Article 93 of the CIT Act; expenses attributable to the domestic business place are deductible within the arm's length limit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Credits and Special Deductions (세액공제·감면)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits/deductions claimed under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, including R&D credits, job creation credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign investors should attach evidence of treaty entitlement and the foreign tax credit computation; tax treaty benefit claims require a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Calculated Tax and Local Income Tax Surcharge (산출세액 및 지방소득세)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at the progressive brackets and the separately imposed 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean branch of a foreign corporation, the surtax is assessed on the branch taxable income attributable to the Korean place of business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Any additional tax from late filing, under-reporting, and non-payment computed in the return or later assessed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are equally subject to penalty taxes; a valid treaty application does not waive domestic procedural penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: additional 20% of the tax payable where the return is filed after one month from the statutory deadline (10% if filed within one month); late payment: surcharge of 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount (approx. 8.03% per annum); under-reporting: 10% of the understated tax (40% for intentional concealment); non-submission or negligence penalties on transfer pricing documentation may add up to 30% of the adjusted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on gross dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder (20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced or exempt rate under a double tax agreement, the Korean payor must withhold at the treaty rate where the foreign recipient submits before the payment date: (i) an Application for Reduction/Exemption of Withholding Tax, (ii) a Certificate of Residence (Tax Residency Certificate, TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, and (iii) a declaration of beneficial ownership; where excess tax is withheld, the foreign corporation may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within 3 years of the end of the filing year, using the same treaty-evidence bundle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate for both royalties and interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local income tax surtax); typical DTA relief under Korean treaties reduces interest to 10% and royalties to 10%-15% (e.g., the Korean-US treaty provides 10% for industrial royalties and certain intercompany interest, with conditions for a 5% dividend rate on substantial shareholdings).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where the aggregate value of cross-border transactions with foreign related parties in a fiscal year exceeds KRW 5,000,000,000; Master File is further required where the multinational group's annual consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000; Country-by-Country Report filing applies to groups whose consolidated annual revenue reaches KRW 100,000,000,000; documentation must be delivered to the National Tax Service within 30 days following a formal request (and no later than 45 days from the corporate tax return filing deadline).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the NTS applies strict substance-over-form doctrine, GAAR under CIT Act Article 52, and the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) provision in bilateral tax treaties; an e-commerce Chusik Hoesa relying on treaty benefits for cross-border royalties or dividends must evidence real economic operations including substantive board decision-making, employees with managerial authority in Korea, physical office/trading premises, and proportionate profit-generating functions, failing which the tax authority may recharacterize the entity as a conduit and deny treaty relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of online retail turnover, such as omitting overseas camping-gear sales settled through PayPal or Stripe, fabricating purchase invoices, or channeling e-commerce receipts through personal accounts of the director.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and monetary fine up to 5 times the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act; civil penalty taxes of 40% of the concealed amount plus late-payment surcharge of 0.022% per day; NTS seizure and public delinquency listing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative director and responsible accounting director are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax; criminal conviction results in imprisonment, travel ban, disqualification as director, and restitution of evaded taxes through asset tracing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, e.g., inflating fees paid to an overseas affiliate for e-commerce platform services or IP licensing to shift Korean profit abroad, or failing to submit Local File/Master File when the statutory thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment of the Korean taxable income; additional tax penalty up to 30% of the adjusted tax differential under the Law on International Tax Coordination, plus interest; denial of related-party expense deductions; the NTS may also assess the foreign related party's deemed Korean income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally subject to civil restitution where transfer pricing manipulation is held to constitute gross negligence; criminal referral for fraudulent transfer pricing attracts imprisonment up to 5 years and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a conduit lacking real employees, premises, board operations, and revenue-generating functions while claiming treaty benefits or favorable holding-company treatment for the outdoor e-commerce business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and disregarding of the entity under CIT Act Article 52 GAAR and the substance-over-form doctrine; retrocrative re-assessment of Korean-source income at full statutory rates; denial of treaty reductions under the Principal Purpose Test; disgorgement of preferential tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the shell is used for tax evasion, rendering the incorporating shareholders and directors personally liable for all assessed taxes, penalties, and interest; criminal sanctions include imprisonment and travel/prohibition orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting PayPal/Stripe settlement flows without customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions connected with high-value outdoor equipment sales to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), or maintaining anonymous/dormant merchant accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, failure to report suspicious transactions: imprisonment up to 3 years and criminal fine up to KRW 30 million; administrative fines up to KRW 50 million and revocation of electronic payment processing licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director responsible for AML governance and compliance officers face personal criminal prosecution, monetary fines, and travel restrictions during pending investigations; repeated violations trigger permanent disqualification from financial services management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Disclose Foreign Financial Accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining offshore merchant, PayPal, or Stripe settlement accounts with year-end aggregate balances exceeding KRW 500,000,000 and failing to file the Foreign Financial Account Report with the National Tax Service by 30 June of the following year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty tax of 20% of the unreported balance under Article 8 of the Law on International Tax Coordination; where unreported amounts exceed KRW 5,000,000,000, criminal referral with imprisonment of up to 2 years and fines; overlapping addition of 0.022% daily surcharge where tax was underpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The controlling shareholder, representative director, and any signatory on the undisclosed foreign account are jointly personally liable; NTS enforcement includes travel bans, property attachment, and criminal imprisonment for willful non-disclosure.
